notes.meaning: True wisdom is very rare, but it is of great value. It softens a person's character, changing a harsh or proud look into one that is gentle, cheerful, and humble. It also gives insight to understand hard matters and explain God's word and work to others.

God's people are instructed to obey the governing king. This loyalty is a religious duty because an oath of allegiance has been made in the presence of God. Keeping our promises honors the order God has placed over us in this world.

differ.view: The oath means a general vow to obey all of God's laws, and obeying leaders is simply one part of that wider duty.

notes.meaning: Do not rush out from the king's presence in anger, and do not join in any evil plot or rebellion against him. A ruler holds supreme power and can punish those who cross him, so no ordinary subject can question his authority. It is dangerous to challenge absolute power.
Obeying lawful commands keeps a person safe from harm. A wise person learns the right time and the right way to act and speak. Knowing how to handle delicate moments brings success and peace.

differ.view: The commandment here refers to God's law rather than the king's order, teaching that the wise know how and when to obey the Lord.

notes.meaning: God has appointed a fitting time and manner for every purpose, but people suffer greatly because they cannot see what lies ahead. Since no one knows the future, people often miss the best moment to act and walk into trouble unawares.

Just as a person cannot hold back the wind or the breath of life, no one can delay the day of death. Death is a war where no soldier receives a discharge or substitute. Wickedness and human schemes cannot rescue anyone when that final hour arrives.

Rulers often abuse their authority to dominate and oppress other people. This tyrannical rule harms the innocent subjects, but it also ruins the ruler himself by bringing down God's eventual judgment.

Wicked rulers who frequented sacred courts were given grand burials, while their evil deeds were quickly forgotten by the city. Meanwhile, good and faithful people were driven away and ignored. This unfairness in earthly honor is another painful picture of the world's brokenness.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Ancient Catholic readings using the Latin Vulgate saw the verse as describing hypocrites who are praised in life and hidden inside a peaceful Church.

notes.meaning: When God delays carrying out the punishment for wrongdoing, people mistakenly think He does not care. They take His patience as permission to sin more boldly and harden their hearts in evil. Even so, God's justice is never forgotten; it is only waiting.

A sinner may commit evil many times and still seem to live a long life, but real lasting peace belongs only to those who honor God. The wicked have no true fear of God, so their days are ultimately empty and fleeting like a passing shadow. God will surely make things right in the end.

Life on earth often seems backwards and deeply confusing. Righteous people frequently suffer the hardships that wicked people deserve, while evil people enjoy the prosperity meant for the good. This mismatch shows how empty and fallen this present world is.

In light of life's confusing trials, a person should gratefully enjoy the daily blessings God gives, such as simple food, drink, and honest work. This cheerfulness is not wild sinful partying, but a quiet, thankful heart trusting in God's daily care.

differ.view: This call to eat and drink expresses the voice of an ungodly, sensual seeker rather than godly counsel.

notes.meaning: Even if someone studies day and night without sleep, no human being can fully figure out everything God does under the sun. God's plans and providence are too deep for our limited minds. Rather than wearing ourselves out trying to solve every mystery, we are called to trust Him and submit to His will.
